title: Computer organization and architecture
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Understand how computers execute programs: integer and floating-point representation, Boolean logic and digital circuits, instruction set architecture and RISC-V assembly language, functions and the stack, the processor datapath, pipelining, the memory hierarchy and caches, and performance.

blocks.deliverable: Convert and add numbers in several representations.
Design an adder and a register from gates.
Write and trace three RISC-V programs.
Week 7 midterm; translate a C function into RISC-V.
Draw a pipeline diagram with forwarding.
Simulate a cache on an address trace.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Write a simulator in Python for a subset of RISC-V (registers, memory, arithmetic, loads and stores, and branches), run supplied programs on it, and add a direct-mapped cache model that reports hit rates.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
